title: Tutorial: Fitting Robust Nonlinear Mixed Effects Models
text: Nonlinear mixed effects models (NLME) commonly used analyzing longitudinal data observations collected repeatedly multiple subjects. models allow population-level effects estimated accounting subject-specific variation random effects. However, traditional NLME models typically assume variability measurements constant across subjects time. many applications, assumption unrealistic. example, biological measurements may different levels variability depending patient characteristics latent processes. JMVN package extends nonlinear mixed effects modeling allowing flexible dispersion models. tutorial demonstrates fit: standard nonlinear mixed effects model. two-step approach auxiliary longitudinal process first estimated incorporated variance model. joint modeling approach processes estimated simultaneously.

title: Tutorial: Fitting Robust Nonlinear Mixed Effects Models
text: example dataset contains repeated measurements 100 individuals. individual 15 longitudinal observations. variables : patid: patient identifier day: observation time lgcopy: primary longitudinal response cd4: auxiliary longitudinal measurement
code: #### Read in the data simdat <- readRDS(here::here("inst/extdata","toy_data.rds"))  # 100 unique patients # 15 repeated measurements per patient # var: patid, day, lgcopy, cd4

title: Tutorial: Fitting Robust Nonlinear Mixed Effects Models
text: first define two nonlinear functions. first function describes exponential decay trajectory: f(t)=p1+p2e−p3t f(t)=p_1+p_2e^{-p_3t} second function describes quadratic trajectory: f(t)=p1+p2t+p3t2 f(t)=p_1+p_2t+p_3t^2 functions used specify nonlinear mean structures.
code: #### pre-define the functions we need for modeling     nf1 <- function(p1,p2,p3,t) p1+p2*exp(-p3*t)     nf2 <- function(p1,p2,p3,t) p1+p2*t+p3*t^2

title: Tutorial: Fitting Robust Nonlinear Mixed Effects Models
text: fitting robust dispersion models, first fit conventional nonlinear mixed effects model using nlme(). model provides initial parameter estimates subsequent models.
code: #### LB method: nlme()     cat("--Fit NLME() \n") #> --Fit NLME()     dat_g <- groupedData(lgcopy~day|patid, data=simdat)             start0 <- c(p1=1,p2=2,p3=3) # random starting values     nls.fit  <- nls(lgcopy~nf1(p1,p2,p3, day), data=dat_g, start=start0)     start <- coef(nls.fit) # update starting values     nlme.fit <- R.utils::withTimeout({try(nlme(lgcopy~nf1(p1,p2,p3, day),fixed = p1+p2+p3 ~1,random  = p1+p3 ~1,                      data=dat_g,start=start))},timeout=1.5,onTimeout="warning") #> Warning in nlme.formula(lgcopy ~ nf1(p1, p2, p3, day), fixed = p1 + p2 + : #> Iteration 1, LME step: nlminb() did not converge (code = 1). Do increase #> 'msMaxIter'!

title: Tutorial: Fitting Robust Nonlinear Mixed Effects Models
text: two-step approach separates estimation auxiliary process nonlinear response model. first step estimates latent CD4 trajectory. predicted CD4 values used dispersion model nonlinear response.

title: Tutorial: Fitting Robust Nonlinear Mixed Effects Models
code: #### TS method:     cat("--Runing Two-step model\n") #> --Runing Two-step model      # step 1: fit CD4 model and get predicted true CD4 values          cd4.fit <- try(lme(cd4~day+I(day^2), data=simdat, random=~1|patid))     simdat$cd4.pred <- fitted(cd4.fit)

what: Step 2: Fit the Joint Mean-Variance Model
title: Tutorial: Fitting Robust Nonlinear Mixed Effects Models
text: variance model allows measurement variability depend estimated CD4 trajectory. nonlinear response model specified .
code: # step 2: Joint modeling mean and variance for NLME          # variance model:       sigmaObject_TS <- list(model=~1+cd4.pred+(1|patid),                            link='log',                            ran.dist="normal",                            str.fixed=c(2*log(nlme.fit$sigma), 0),                            lower.fixed=NULL,                            upper.fixed=NULL,                            fixName="alpha",                            ranName="a",                            dispName="siga",                            str.disp=0.5) # mean model     nlmeObject_TS <- list(nf = "nf1",                           model= lgcopy ~ nf(p1,p2,p3,day),                           var=c("day"),                           fixed = p1+p2+p3 ~1,                           random = p1+p3 ~1,                           family='normal',                            ran.dist='normal',                           fixName="beta",                           ranName="u",                           dispName="d",                           sigma=sigmaObject_TS,                           ran.Cov=NULL,                           str.fixed=fixef(nlme.fit),                           str.disp=as.numeric(VarCorr(nlme.fit)[,"StdDev"][c("p1", "p3")]),                           lower.fixed=NULL,                           upper.fixed=rep(100,3),                           lower.disp=c(0,0),                           upper.disp=c(Inf,Inf)                           )          nlmeObjects_TS=list(nlmeObject_TS)          TS <- try(Rnlme(nlmeObjects=nlmeObjects_TS, long.data=simdat,                          idVar="patid", sd.method="HL", dispersion.SD = TRUE,                         independent.raneff=FALSE)) #> Error in str_trim(resp) : could not find function "str_trim"

title: Tutorial: Fitting Robust Nonlinear Mixed Effects Models
text: joint modeling approach simultaneously estimates: nonlinear response model, auxiliary longitudinal model, measurement error model, dispersion model. Unlike two-step approach, uncertainty latent CD4 trajectory propagated entire estimation procedure. CD4 measurement model specified first. measurement error model defined . Finally, models fitted simultaneously.
code: #### JM method     cat("--Runing Joint model\n") #> --Runing Joint model #### JM     sigma1 <- list(model=NULL,                    str.disp=as.numeric(VarCorr(cd4.fit)[,"StdDev"][2]),                    lower.disp=NULL,                    upper.disp=NULL,                    parName="xi") lmeObject_JM <- list(nf = "nf2" ,                          model= cd4 ~ nf(p1,p2,p3,day),                          var=c("day"),                          fixed = p1+p2+p3 ~1,                          random = p1 ~1,                          family='normal',                           ran.dist='normal',                          fixName="gamma",                          ranName="b",                          dispName="sigb",                          sigma=sigma1,                          ran.Cov=NULL,                          str.fixed=fixef(cd4.fit),                          str.disp=as.numeric(VarCorr(cd4.fit)[,"StdDev"][1]),                          lower.fixed=NULL,                          upper.fixed=rep(100,3),                          lower.disp=c(0),                          upper.disp=c(Inf)                          ) sigma2 <- list(model=~1+cd4.true+(1|patid),                    link='log',                    ran.dist="normal",                    str.fixed=c(2*log(nlme.fit$sigma), 0),                    lower.fixed=NULL,                    upper.fixed=NULL,                    fixName="alpha",                    ranName="a",                    dispName="siga",                    str.disp=0.5,                    trueVal.model=list(var="cd4.true", model=lmeObject_JM)                    ) # variance model nlmeObject_JM <- list(nf = "nf1",                           model= lgcopy ~ nf(p1,p2,p3,day),                           var=c("day"),                           fixed = p1+p2+p3 ~1,                           random = p1+p3 ~1,                           family='normal',                            ran.dist='normal',                           fixName="beta",                           ranName="u",                           dispName="d",                           sigma=sigma2,                           ran.Cov=NULL,                           str.fixed=fixef(nlme.fit),                           str.disp=as.numeric(VarCorr(nlme.fit)[,"StdDev"][c("p1", "p3")]),                           lower.fixed=NULL,                           upper.fixed=rep(100,3),                           lower.disp=c(0,0),                           upper.disp=c(Inf,Inf)                           )          nlmeObjects_JM <- list(nlmeObject_JM, lmeObject_JM)          JM <- try(Rnlme(nlmeObjects=nlmeObjects_JM, long.data=simdat,                      idVar="patid", sd.method="HL", dispersion.SD = TRUE,                     independent.raneff="byModel")) #> Error in str_trim(resp) : could not find function "str_trim"     saveRDS(JM, file = "JM.rds")

title: Joint nonlinear mixed-effects model estimation (Rnlme) — Rnlme
text: nlmeObjects nonlinear mixed-effects model object containing model specifications. long.data longitudinal dataset containing observations grouping information. idVar Character string specifying subject/group identifier variable. sd.method Method estimating standard errors. Options "None", "HL". Default "None". dispersion.SD Logical indicating whether dispersion parameter standard errors estimated. Default FALSE. independent.raneff Logical indicating whether random effects assumed independent. Default FALSE. sdghsize Number quadrature points adaptive Gaussian quadrature. Default 4. itertol Likelihood convergence tolerance. Default 0.001. Ptol Parameter convergence tolerance. Default 0.01. iterMax Maximum number iterations. Default 15. Verbose Logical indicating whether progress messages printed. Default FALSE.
